facts.facts_role: Information architecture, event templates, hosting plan
facts.facts_status: Self-directed concept / not a live client engagement

brief.brief_heading: A real-world problem, not a feature wishlist.
brief.brief_text: The fictional starting point is an organization sharing event details in image flyers and long announcement feeds. Dates, venue changes, accessibility information, and registration links are difficult to scan. Once an event has passed, old details can still look current.
brief.brief_objective: Help residents find a current event and understand how to attend.
brief.brief_boundary: Updates must be manageable by volunteers with limited time.

discovery.discovery_heading: Understand the journey before drawing the screens.
discovery.discovery_text: The proposed discovery centers on a resident checking an event on a phone, a volunteer posting a change, and a coordinator maintaining the calendar. The core questions are simple: what is happening, when is it, where do I go, and do I need to book? Those answers should not require reading a flyer image.
discovery.discovery_direction: Upcoming events become structured pages rather than unorganized posts. Each event includes a date, time zone, venue, attendance instructions, access information, and an optional registration link. Past events move into an archive. A cancellation or venue change is visible near the title instead of being buried in the body.

decisions.decisions_decision_1_heading: Treat dates as information, not decoration
decisions.decisions_decision_1_text: Date and location appear as selectable text. Event titles link to permanent detail pages, giving people something reliable to share.
decisions.decisions_decision_2_text: Cancelled or rescheduled events retain their URLs and show a prominent status notice. Volunteers do not have to delete the record and break shared links.
decisions.decisions_decision_3_text: The hosting specification identifies who can publish, who handles renewals, and how the site can be restored or transferred to a new maintainer.

examples.examples_heading: From a vague starting point to a clearer experience.
examples.examples_intro: This comparison describes the fictional starting scenario and the proposed design direction. It is not a claim about an existing client website.
examples.examples_before_1: Critical event details embedded in flyers.
examples.examples_before_2: Old and upcoming announcements mixed together.
examples.examples_before_3: Publishing knowledge held by a single volunteer.
examples.examples_after_1: A consistent event summary before the narrative.
examples.examples_after_2: Separate upcoming and past event collections.
examples.examples_after_3: A documented publishing and recovery checklist.
examples.examples_detail_heading: An event page that answers the practical questions
examples.examples_detail_text: The sample event pattern places title, attendance status, date, venue, and booking requirements together. Access notes describe the entrance, seating, and who to contact about accommodations. A flyer can still appear as supporting artwork, but its information is also available as text. A changed venue gets a dated notice near the top.
examples.examples_mobile_heading: What changes on a smaller screen?
examples.examples_mobile_text: Event summaries stack in date order, with location and attendance instructions immediately below the title. Long venue names wrap. A status notice remains above the details, and a flyer never becomes the only source of essential information.

detail_image.detail_image_alt: Illustrative Northline Community interface concept, not a live client screenshot
detail_image.detail_image_caption: Layout study: event information available as text. The controls shown are illustration, not an interactive application.

implementation.implementation_text: The recommended implementation generates static pages from structured event content. Sorting uses complete timestamps and an explicit time zone, not the server’s assumed local time. Build validation flags missing dates or booking URLs. The hosting plan includes HTTPS, redirect rules, monitored renewals, and backups of source content as well as deployable output. These are proposed implementation details, not claims about a live deployed client site.
implementation.implementation_edge_cases_heading: The awkward cases belong in the plan.
implementation.implementation_edge_cases_text: Multi-day events need an end date, not a guessed expiry time. Cancelled events should not disappear without explanation. A missing flyer should not remove the date or registration instructions. External booking links need a clear destination and should not be styled as if registration takes place on this site.
implementation.implementation_check_1: Review the critical journey on a small phone, tablet, and desktop.
implementation.implementation_check_2: Check keyboard order, visible focus, contrast, and meaningful image descriptions.
implementation.implementation_check_3: Exercise long content, missing optional fields, and invalid input states.
implementation.implementation_check_4: Verify every route, external destination, and recovery or escalation path.
implementation.implementation_verification_note: This is the proposed acceptance checklist for the concept, not a report of a commissioned production release.

handoff.handoff_heading: Make the next update as considered as the first.
handoff.handoff_text: A polished launch is only part of the job. The proposed handoff explains what can be changed safely, what needs specialist help, and who owns the important accounts. Documentation should let a new maintainer understand the system without reconstructing the project from messages.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_1: Upcoming and past event list specifications.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_3: A volunteer-friendly content and publishing checklist.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_4: Ownership, backup, restore, and renewal responsibilities.
handoff.handoff_phase_1_text: agree on the audience, scope, responsibilities, and acceptance criteria.
handoff.handoff_phase_2_text: review structure, realistic content, and the critical interaction states.
handoff.handoff_phase_3_text: implement the agreed patterns and record any decisions that affect maintenance.
handoff.handoff_phase_4_text: work through the checklist, resolve issues, and rehearse handoff.

outcomes.outcomes_heading: Measure what matters. Don’t invent the numbers.
outcomes.outcomes_text: For a real release, test whether a resident can locate an upcoming event, identify its venue, and find registration instructions without assistance. Monitor stale information and publishing errors as well as traffic. Success includes easier maintenance, not only more page views.
outcomes.outcomes_evidence_text: The proposed structure, original interface illustration, content patterns, and implementation reasoning show how this project could be approached. No conversion uplift, revenue increase, saved hours, or client testimonial is claimed.

lessons.lessons_heading: Useful information deserves a dependable home.
lessons.lessons_text: The most useful community website is often the one that makes ordinary information easy to trust—and easy for the next volunteer to maintain.

cover.cover_caption: Maple Street Workshop / original interface concept, shown for illustration.

facts.facts_role: Content strategy, website design, front-end development
facts.facts_status: Self-directed concept / not a live client engagement

brief.brief_heading: A real-world problem, not a feature wishlist.
brief.brief_text: The starting scenario is a workshop whose best work lives on social media. Prospective customers see beautiful furniture, but cannot easily answer practical questions: what commissions are accepted, how a project begins, or what information to send. The owner ends up answering those same questions individually.
brief.brief_objective: Help a prospective customer understand the work and send a useful project inquiry.
brief.brief_boundary: A small team needs to update projects without maintaining a complicated application.

discovery.discovery_heading: Understand the journey before drawing the screens.
discovery.discovery_text: The concept starts with three customer journeys: a homeowner exploring a custom dining table, a designer looking for a fabrication partner, and a previous customer returning for care advice. Each needs different details, but all should be able to find a service explanation and a clear next step without knowing the workshop’s internal terminology.
discovery.discovery_direction: The proposed site separates Work, Services, Our Workshop, and Start a Project. Project pages explain the brief, material choices, constraints, and finished details. Service pages explain the commission process before asking for an inquiry. Care information sits outside the sales journey so returning customers do not have to start over.

decisions.decisions_decision_1_text: Large project images sit beside concise explanations of the problem each piece solves. Instead of a gallery with no context, each project tells a short story about use, material, and craft.
decisions.decisions_decision_2_heading: Ask better questions, not more questions
decisions.decisions_decision_2_text: The proposed inquiry flow asks for project type, approximate dimensions, timing, and contact details. Budget guidance is optional. Every field has a reason, and a successful submission would explain what happens next.
decisions.decisions_decision_3_text: A small set of page patterns gives the owner a repeatable way to add projects. Titles, cover images, captions, and project facts use consistent positions rather than requiring a new layout for every update.

examples.examples_heading: From a vague starting point to a clearer experience.
examples.examples_intro: This comparison describes the fictional starting scenario and the proposed design direction. It is not a claim about an existing client website.
examples.examples_before_1: A gallery with little explanation of the service.
examples.examples_before_2: A generic “Contact us” link after a long scroll.
examples.examples_before_3: Key project information scattered across captions.
examples.examples_after_1: Project stories connect visual detail to customer needs.
examples.examples_after_2: A visible “Start a project” path from each service.
examples.examples_after_3: A consistent brief, materials, and process summary.
examples.examples_detail_heading: An inquiry that starts a useful conversation
examples.examples_detail_text: Instead of “Tell us more,” the example brief asks: What would you like made? Where will it be used? Do you have approximate dimensions? Is there a date you are working toward? A short note explains that a rough idea is enough for a first conversation. This lowers the pressure without hiding the information the workshop needs.
examples.examples_mobile_heading: What changes on a smaller screen?
examples.examples_mobile_text: Project photography moves above its supporting copy, while service details keep their natural reading order. The inquiry path stays easy to reach without covering the work. Captions and material notes remain text, not tiny labels baked into images.

detail_image.detail_image_alt: Illustrative Maple Street Workshop interface concept, not a live client screenshot
detail_image.detail_image_caption: Layout study: a project-led homepage with a specific next step. The controls shown are illustration, not an interactive application.

implementation.implementation_text: The implementation approach uses a static-first page structure and reusable project records. Images have explicit dimensions, responsive sources, meaningful alternative text, and lazy loading below the first screen. Essential navigation and project content remain available without JavaScript. A real inquiry form would require a separately configured server-side endpoint with validation, spam controls, and clear delivery monitoring; this concept does not pretend to submit requests.
implementation.implementation_edge_cases_heading: The awkward cases belong in the plan.
implementation.implementation_edge_cases_text: Long project names wrap naturally. Missing secondary photography does not leave an empty gallery. The inquiry confirmation and error states are part of the specification rather than last-minute additions. A honeypot alone would not be treated as sufficient protection for a live contact endpoint.

handoff.handoff_heading: Make the next update as considered as the first.
handoff.handoff_text: A polished launch is only part of the job. The proposed handoff explains what can be changed safely, what needs specialist help, and who owns the important accounts. Documentation should let a new maintainer understand the system without reconstructing the project from messages.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_1: A page inventory and agreed content hierarchy.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_2: Homepage, service, project, and inquiry layout specifications.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_3: A reusable project-content checklist and image guidance.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_4: A launch checklist covering links, metadata, form delivery, and ownership.

handoff.handoff_phase_2_text: review structure, realistic content, and the critical interaction states.
handoff.handoff_phase_3_text: implement the agreed patterns and record any decisions that affect maintenance.

outcomes.outcomes_heading: Measure what matters. Don’t invent the numbers.
outcomes.outcomes_text: For a real launch, establish a baseline for inquiry quality, service-to-contact journeys, and avoidable clarification emails. Review anonymized patterns rather than collecting unnecessary personal data. A rise in raw submissions would not, by itself, prove that the design helped.
outcomes.outcomes_evidence_text: The proposed structure, original interface illustration, content patterns, and implementation reasoning show how this project could be approached. No conversion uplift, revenue increase, saved hours, or client testimonial is claimed.

lessons.lessons_text: A portfolio should do more than show that something looks good. Give the work enough context that a customer can recognize their own needs in it.

cover.cover_caption: Fieldnote Operations / original interface concept, shown for illustration.

facts.facts_role: Workflow mapping, intake design, human-reviewed automation
facts.facts_status: Self-directed concept / not a live client engagement

brief.brief_heading: A real-world problem, not a feature wishlist.
brief.brief_text: In this fictional scenario, requests arrive through several channels and the team copies information between an inbox, notes, and a task board. The pain is not simply typing. It is unclear ownership: nobody knows whether a request has been checked, assigned, or answered. Automating that confusion would only make it move faster.
brief.brief_objective: Turn an incoming request into an organized, reviewable next step.
brief.brief_boundary: No autonomous sending, quoting, or changes to customer records.

discovery.discovery_heading: Understand the journey before drawing the screens.
discovery.discovery_text: The proposed discovery follows a request from arrival to response. It identifies the minimum information needed, the person responsible for each decision, and the places where the team currently has to interpret missing context. Routine routing is separated from decisions that affect pricing, promises, or customer relationships.
discovery.discovery_direction: The proposed workflow has four explicit states: Received, Needs Context, Ready for Review, and Approved. Each request has a source reference and an owner. Automation can prepare a summary and suggested response, but a reviewer decides whether it is accurate and appropriate before anything leaves the system.

decisions.decisions_decision_1_text: The first version handles only a defined request type. Unknown requests go to manual triage rather than being forced into the nearest category.
decisions.decisions_decision_2_text: The review screen shows the source message beside the summary and draft. A person can edit, reject, or request more context instead of approving a black box.
decisions.decisions_decision_3_heading: Build a stop button into the process
decisions.decisions_decision_3_text: The automation can be paused without losing the incoming request. Manual handling remains a supported path, not a failure state.

examples.examples_heading: From a vague starting point to a clearer experience.
examples.examples_intro: This comparison describes the fictional starting scenario and the proposed design direction. It is not a claim about an existing client website.
examples.examples_before_1: Requests copied into different personal notes.
examples.examples_before_2: A draft can be mistaken for a sent response.
examples.examples_after_1: One request record with an owner and source link.
examples.examples_after_2: Draft, approved, and sent are distinct states.
examples.examples_after_3: Missing information routes to a visible review queue.
examples.examples_detail_heading: A reviewable draft, not an autonomous promise
examples.examples_detail_text: An example request says: “We need help updating the booking page before an event.” The draft summary records the affected page, desired change, and event date if supplied. If the date is missing, it is flagged—not guessed. A suggested response asks for the missing context and avoids inventing a price, delivery date, or confirmed scope.
examples.examples_mobile_heading: What changes on a smaller screen?
examples.examples_mobile_text: Queue columns become a single ordered list. Status and ownership stay next to the request title. The reviewer opens one record at a time, keeping the original message and draft together rather than squeezing two unreadable panels onto a phone.

detail_image.detail_image_alt: Illustrative Fieldnote Operations interface concept, not a live client screenshot
detail_image.detail_image_caption: Layout study: a visible review queue with distinct states. The controls shown are illustration, not an interactive application.

implementation.implementation_text: The design specifies a durable queue, idempotency keys for duplicate events, structured output validation, and a separate approval record. Access is limited to the minimum required source data. Any eventual send action must check that the current draft version was approved, so editing a previously approved draft invalidates its approval. This page documents a concept; no live mailbox or third-party automation is connected.
implementation.implementation_edge_cases_heading: The awkward cases belong in the plan.
implementation.implementation_edge_cases_text: Duplicate events should resolve to the existing request. Unrecognized attachments are held for review rather than automatically executed or interpreted as trusted instructions. Provider timeouts move work into a retryable state with a visible error. Customer text is treated as untrusted input, not permission to change the workflow or access other records.

implementation.implementation_check_2: Check keyboard order, visible focus, contrast, and meaningful image descriptions.
implementation.implementation_check_3: Exercise long content, missing optional fields, and invalid input states.
implementation.implementation_check_4: Verify every route, external destination, and recovery or escalation path.
implementation.implementation_verification_note: This is the proposed acceptance checklist for the concept, not a report of a commissioned production release.

handoff.handoff_heading: Make the next update as considered as the first.
handoff.handoff_text: A polished launch is only part of the job. The proposed handoff explains what can be changed safely, what needs specialist help, and who owns the important accounts. Documentation should let a new maintainer understand the system without reconstructing the project from messages.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_1: Workflow and ownership map with approved boundaries.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_2: Request schema, review states, and example drafts.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_3: Test fixtures for missing, duplicated, and unexpected inputs.
handoff.handoff_deliverable_4: Pause, retry, escalation, and access-revocation procedures.

handoff.handoff_phase_2_text: review structure, realistic content, and the critical interaction states.
handoff.handoff_phase_3_text: implement the agreed patterns and record any decisions that affect maintenance.

outcomes.outcomes_heading: Measure what matters. Don’t invent the numbers.
outcomes.outcomes_text: A real pilot would compare time spent reviewing drafts against manual handling, track correction rates, and check whether requests are consistently assigned. The evaluation should count rework and supervision time rather than reporting only how many drafts were generated.
outcomes.outcomes_evidence_text: The proposed structure, original interface illustration, content patterns, and implementation reasoning show how this project could be approached. No conversion uplift, revenue increase, saved hours, or client testimonial is claimed.

lessons.lessons_heading: A good system keeps people in control.
lessons.lessons_text: Useful automation makes responsibility clearer. A shorter workflow is not an improvement if nobody can tell what happened or who approved it.
